The test image shows a coffee leaf with a large, irregular brown/necrotic patch covering a significant portion of the leaf. The tissue is dead and dried with an irregular boundary against green healthy tissue. No circular spots, no yellow/orange powder, no visible trails.

This large irregular necrotic patch pattern most closely matches **Miner** (large necrotic patches from larval mining) or potentially **Phoma** (dark lesions on leaves). Let me view one Miner reference image to confirm.

The Miner reference shows a smaller brown spot with irregular edges. The test image has a much larger necrotic area, but the Miner description explicitly mentions "large necrotic patches caused by larval mining" as an advanced stage.

Comparing all candidates:
- **Miner**: Large irregular necrotic patches — matches the test image well
- **Phoma**: Circular dark spots up to 2cm — the test lesion is larger and not circular
- **Rust**: Orange/yellow powder on leaf underside — not present
- **Brown_Eye_Spot / Berry_Blotch**: Small circular spots with grey centers — not present
- **Cerscospora**: No distinctive markers visible matching this

The large, irregular, dry brown necrotic patch on the upper leaf surface is most consistent with advanced Miner damage.
